clue.text: Insects found in journeys across hospital

indicators.note: the journeys stretch across the hospital letter, so one word is laid around the other

parts.note: journeys are trips
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Bugs turn up on someone's travels that pass by a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: These are tiny winged plant pests, sometimes called thunderflies, so they are a kind of insect.

clue.text: Excited girl being heard — one that laughs?

indicators.note: being heard tells us the words are to be taken by their sound when spoken

parts.note: excited can mean high, as in high spirits; Ena is a girl's name, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: An overexcited girl is audible: is she the one who keeps giggling?
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH ENA, spoken, sounds like the animal's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted species of this African scavenger is famous for a call that sounds like cackling laughter.

clue.text: Smashing beer — I ain't drunk!

indicators.note: smashing breaks the words apart so their letters can be reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: A drinker protests, after praising the beer, that they are perfectly sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' looks like praise for the beer but signals the anagram of BEER and IAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective or noun this is a formal word for someone intoxicated, a synonym of drunk.

clue.text: Islander's boat lacking power carries nothing

definitions.note: read as 'Islander is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: the shortened boat carries the nothing within it
lacking means a letter is dropped from the boat

parts.note: a sampan is a flat-bottomed Asian boat
P is the abbreviation for power in physics
O, the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: A Pacific island's little boat, its engine gone, holds no cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking power' takes P out of SAMPAN to leave SAMAN, and O goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Samoa in the South Pacific is a native of those islands, so an islander.

clue.text: Spooner's natural group is refined

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the initial sounds of the two pieces trade places

parts.note: gut as in a gut reaction, instinctive and natural
a class is a group

explanation.surface: A clumsy cleric declares that a group of naturals is genteel.
explanation.walkthrough: GUT CLASS with G and C swapped gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-glass accent is a very upper-class, polished way of speaking, hence refined.

clue.text: One may be responsible for restoration of Victorian stones

definitions.text: One may be responsible for restoration of Victorian stones

indicators.note: restoration rebuilds the words, so their letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Who looks after repairs to old Victorian masonry?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and anagram of VICTORIAN STONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone working to preserve heritage buildings or nature would oversee repairs of old stonework.

clue.text: Around one get everyone to scamper up for omelette

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to scamper is to trot
one is the Roman numeral I

parts.note: everyone is all

explanation.surface: Gather the whole party round one person and get them to run upstairs for an omelette.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'omelette' is the Spanish kind, not the Mexican flatbread of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spain the tortilla is a thick potato and egg omelette, not the Mexican flatbread.

clue.text: Calm, even after an upset

indicators.note: upset turns the word over, and it still reads the same afterwards

parts.note: flat and even

explanation.surface: Someone is steady and composed again following a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for even reads the same when turned backwards, so it survives the upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A calm, composed person is level-headed; a level voice is steady and calm.

clue.text: Church worker's credit is devilishly circumscribed

definitions.note: read as 'Church worker is', the 's a link

indicators.note: the credit and is are circumscribed, drawn round, by the devil

parts.note: devilishly points to Satan, the devil
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchman's credit rating is wickedly limited.
explanation.definitionFit: This officer of a church looks after the vestments and sacred vessels, so is a church worker.

clue.text: Perhaps that put off underground worker

parts.note: to put off is to deter
a miner works underground

explanation.surface: Something seemingly deterred a man who works down a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is not a link word but the thing defined, a grammatical example.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'that' in 'that dog' is an example of the word class that limits a noun.

clue.text: Wrong opinion denying love

parts.note: to have a voice is to have an opinion
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: It is mistaken to hold a view that rejects love.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is an immoral habit, a moral wrong, used here as a noun.

clue.text: Coach's demeanour

definitions.meaning: a coach is a horse-drawn passenger vehicle
demeanour is one's bearing or posture

explanation.surface: A trainer's manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a horse-drawn vehicle and the way a person holds their body.

clue.text: Trendy boy, one gathered, is 'not outstanding'

parts.note: a lad is a boy
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is wry: inlaid work is set flush, so it does not stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlay is set into a surface so it lies flush, literally not standing out from it.

clue.text: A backing group — it's hairy

indicators.note: the A comes behind, backing up the group

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A supporting band is described as long-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology this is a bristle or stiff hair on an animal or plant, so a hairy thing.

clue.text: Kill time then prescribe little time's to be wasted

explanation.walkthrough: Taking T from DICTATE leaves DICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out or destroy completely, a strong synonym for killing off.

clue.text: Little woman I go out with and stand by

parts.note: Val is short for Valerie, a woman's name made little
to go out with someone is to date them

explanation.surface: A wife says she will date and stay loyal to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To validate a claim is to support or confirm it, to stand by it.

clue.text: Series of events Irish town cut short a month earlier

clue.text: One sees lots of pictures where the altar is in church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

clue.text: Prepare to go up or down for surgical treatment

clue.text: Staff employed by American entertainer

clue.text: Sailor buried by offspring, here?

clue.text: One waiting to go to match needs money, having lost note

clue.text: American explorers taking line that's getting up one's nose maybe

clue.text: A hundred up before tea, not a small score?

clue.text: Mostly swamp? It certainly isn't!

clue.text: Bible sh tho 'tricky would be apparent in this test-word

clue.text: The fellow will be leading 5 dn's employer perhaps very resolutely
